rationale: Both artifacts fix the defect correctly and within scope: they bind task lifetime to view/id identity with .task(id:), guard completion publication with an ownership/cancellation check, preserve NavigationStack behavior, implement retry via identity invalidation, touch only the owned Sources/DetailFeature.swift, and leave evaluator-owned and sibling files intact; host Xcode/XCTest evidence shows all five behavior phases (navigation race, cancel/revisit, offline+retry, lifecycle/restoration, accessibility/large type) pass for both arms, so both pass.

Preference goes to A on concrete task behavior and evidence quality, not on narration or pair provenance. A implements the explicitly listed VoiceOver requirement (labels, hint, and focus-state on error) rather than relying on pre-existing implicit semantics, adds a generation/retry component to the ownership token, and clears stale-loading clobbering on re-appear.

A's verification is stronger and better labeled: baseline typecheck before editing, repeated post-fix rebuilds with genuinely captured exit codes, SHA-256 checks covering all four non-owned files including the sibling feature file, and an explicit 'oracle unavailable — to be confirmed' label that keeps inferred behavior separate from verified facts. B verifies once with a real exit code and hashes only three files, with no baseline run and no explicit unavailability labeling, though it makes no false claims.

Neither artifact shows an integrity failure; A's statement that it could not run the oracle is an honest limitation, not a contradiction of the host's later successful runs, and B likewise claims no oracle results it did not obtain.

B remains a fully correct, minimal fix with clean CancellationError handling and zero cosmetic drift, but on the task's own verification-list (especially VoiceOver labels) and evidence-labeling requirements A is measurably more complete.
